title: 1954 Atomic Energy Act moved craft custody to contractor-operated labs

tellings.quote: different mind. I think that craft was moved in 1954 because the 1954 atomic energy agreement gave expanded powers to government-owned contractor operated laboratories like Sandia and so forth to house the craft.

To the extent deemed necessary, the Commission is authorized to make, or to continue in effect, contracts with persons obligating them to produce special nuclear material in facilities owned by the Commission.

plain: The claim is that a recovered UFO craft was moved in 1954 to labs owned by the government but run by private companies, such as Sandia, a US nuclear weapons laboratory. An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb and studies the Pentagon's UFO programs tells Michels this as his own theory. He says the 1954 atomic energy law 'gave expanded powers to government-owned contractor-operated laboratories like Sandia and so forth to house the craft.' He does not say which part of the law he means. The Atomic Energy Act, passed by Congress on August 30, 1954, says at section 41 b. that 'the Commission is authorized to make, or to continue in effect, contracts with persons obligating them to produce special nuclear material in facilities owned by the Commission.' It also allows research contracts for work there, which is the government-owned, contractor-operated arrangement he describes. The act speaks of producing nuclear material and doing research. That such labs were given a craft to keep, and that this is why one moved in 1954, is his step, which the act neither states nor excludes. If true, it would explain how alien hardware ended up with private contractors rather than the government.

discussion.by: Atomic Energy Act of 1954 (Public Law 703, 83rd Congress, 68 Stat. 919)
discussion.text: The teller does not say which provision of the 1954 act he means; if it is section 41 b., the act says "the Commission is authorized to make, or to continue in effect, contracts with persons obligating them to produce special nuclear material in facilities owned by the Commission", and lets it enter "research and development contracts" for work in those facilities, the government-owned, contractor-operated arrangement the teller describes. The act speaks of producing nuclear material and of research there; that such facilities were given a craft to hold, and that this is why a craft moved in 1954, is the teller's step, which the act neither states nor excludes.
